paraphrase: The origin of the body (piṇḍotpatti): from the nameless supreme its own power (nijā śakti) comes forth, and from it the powers Parā, Aparā, Sūkṣmā and Kuṇḍalinī; through them the supreme and cosmic bodies arise, and finally the human body born of the womb.

paraphrase: The knowledge of the body (piṇḍa-vicāra): the nine centres, the sixteen supports, the three aims and the five voids are set out; one who does not rightly know them is a yogī in name only.

paraphrase: The vision of the cosmos in the body (piṇḍa-saṃvitti): the worlds, mountains, rivers, gods and beings are all located within the body, so that the one who knows the body knows the universe.

paraphrase: The support of the body (piṇḍādhāra): the one Śakti — the Lord's own power, called kuṇḍalinī in the body — upholds the body and the cosmos; Śiva and Śakti are not two.

paraphrase: The union of body and supreme state (piṇḍa-pada-samarasa): by the grace of the true guru the body and the supreme state (pada) come to one taste (samarasa); this is attained not by study or reasoning but by the guru.

paraphrase: The marks of the avadhūta yogī: he has shaken off all conventions and bonds, abides in the supreme state, and stands above the other schools and their marks; the Nāth path is presented as including and surpassing them.
